verses.1: Woe to you, city of bloodshed, full of lies, full of violence. You spare no prey.
verses.2: The sound of whips and the sound of clatter, of wheels and galloping horses, and of rattling chariots.
verses.3: The rider goes up, the sword gleams, the spear flashes, and many are the wounded and the heavy fall, with no end to the plunder, and they stagger from the abundance of their plunder.
verses.4: Full of seduction, you are beautiful and adorned with enchantments. You sell nations in your seduction and peoples in your enchantments.
verses.5: Look, I am coming against you, says the LORD of Hosts. I will expose your posterior before you, and I will show nations your disgrace and kingdoms your shame.
verses.6: I will hurl filth upon you, and you will be disgraced and made an example.
verses.7: And everyone who sees you will flee from you and say, "Nineveh has been plundered — who will mourn for her? From where shall I seek comforters for you?"
verses.8: Are you better than No-Amon, who dwelled by the rivers, with water all around her, whose wall was the sea, the river her defense?
verses.9: Cush was her strength and Egypt, yet she too found no end to her flight, and Libya became her help.
verses.10: Even she went into exile as a captive, and her infants were dashed against the top of every street. On her honored ones, lots were cast. All her mighty men were bound in chains.
verses.11: You too will be made drunk, and you will be hidden in the dark. You too will seek a refuge from your enemy.
verses.12: All your strongholds are fig trees with watchtowers. If they shake, they will fall into the mouth of the eater.
verses.13: Look, your people are women in your midst. To your enemies your gates are opened. The fire has consumed your bars.
verses.14: Draw water for the siege, strengthen your strongholds. Go in, press the mud, and mix it with straw. Strengthen the brick.
verses.15: There fire will consume you, the sword will cut you down, it will devour you as the locust, and you will be weighed down like the cankerworm.
verses.16: You have multiplied your traders more than the stars of heaven. The cankerworm spreads and flies.
verses.17: Your guards have fled like the cankerworm, like locusts that alight on a fence in the day of cold when the sun rises and they vanish, and their place is unknown. Woe to them!
verses.18: Your shepherds have lain down, the king of Assyria has put them to sleep. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is none to gather them.
verses.19: No healing is given for your brokenness, no soothing for your wound. All who hear the news of you clap their hands over you. For on whom has your evil not come to pass continually?

notes:
Notes
- v. 4: "Full of seduction" reflects the metaphor of Nineveh as a prostitute (Isa 1:21, etc.), and the term "adorned with enchantments" captures the play on "ba'alat keshefim" — "mistress of enchantments."
- v. 11: "Made drunk" and "hidden in the dark" reflect the Hebrew "tishkari tehi na'alamah," which suggests both a literal and figurative meaning.
- v. 17: "Cankerworm" (arbeh) and "locust" (yalq) are both used in the Hebrew for destructive swarms but are distinguished in the translation to reflect the different species.
